practices.practice: Create and reuse a single, long-lived MongoClient instance per process (do not create a new client per request) to avoid connection churn and pool exhaustion.
practices.prior_belief: Keep a single, long-lived MongoClient instance per process (reuse across requests) and configure an appropriate connection pool (e.g., maxPoolSize) rather than opening/closing clients per request.

practices.practice: Keep connection strings and embedding-provider keys out of source control: read them from environment variables or a secret store (use managed identities / Key Vault for production), and never log secrets.
practices.prior_belief: Store the DOCUMENTDB_URI and any embedding provider keys (OPENAI_API_KEY) only in environment variables or a secret store (e.g., Azure Key Vault); never check connection strings or keys into source control or write them to logs.
practices.source_name: Use Microsoft Entra ID and role-based access control

practices.practice: Always connect using TLS (tls=true) and do not disable certificate verification in production; configure CA path only for local/self-signed scenarios.
practices.prior_belief: Use TLS by default (require TLS/SSL=true in the connection string) and validate server certificates (do not disable certificate verification).

practices.practice: Store embeddings in a dedicated embedding field, normalize vectors when using cosine similarity, and store embedding model name and dimensions with each document so you can detect model drift and re-embed if needed.
practices.prior_belief: Design documents with a dedicated typed embedding field (e.g., embedding: [float32]) and include explicit metadata fields used for filtering (name, indications, dosage) so vector search can be combined with metadata filters; keep embedding dimension constant across all documents.

practices.practice: Create a cosmosSearch vector index (choose DiskANN/HNSW/IVF by scale) with the exact dimensions and similarity used by your embeddings and tune index parameters (maxDegree, lBuild) so nearest-neighbor queries use the vector index instead of scanning the collection.
practices.prior_belief: Create a vector index on the embedding field specifying the appropriate index type and parameters for the workload (algorithm: HNSW or DiskANN, metric: cosine or dot_product, dimension: <embedding_dim>, and tune M/efConstruction/efSearch or equivalent) so nearest-neighbor queries use the vector index instead of full collection scans.

practices.practice: When doing vector k-NN with $search.cosmosSearch, push metadata predicates into the operator's filter (pre-filter) and tune lSearch (ensure lSearch >= k) rather than post-filtering results.
Request a small top-k (e.g., k=10) from the DB, use $project to return only needed fields (and searchScore), and perform any additional re-ranking or business logic in the application layer.
practices.prior_belief: Limit fields returned from DocumentDB queries (projection) to only what the endpoint needs (e.g., name, indications, score) to minimize network IO and deserialization time when returning top-N results.

practices.practice: Create conventional indexes (single-field or compound following ESR: Equality → Sort → Range) on any metadata fields used for filters so hybrid vector+metadata queries are efficient.
practices.prior_belief: Also create conventional indexes on fields used for equality/filtered queries (e.g., name, drug_class, is_active) and on any metadata fields used in combination with vector queries to enable efficient hybrid search filtering.

practices.practice: Run explain()/queryPlanner (or use the MCP tools) after creating indexes and running representative queries to verify the plan uses indexes (no COLLSCAN) and to measure candidate counts and executionStats.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain()/queryPlanner (or the MCP server tools) after creating indexes and running representative vector and metadata queries to verify the query uses the vector index and to measure candidate counts and execution time.

practices.practice: Enable driver retry options (retryReads) for retryable operations and implement application-level exponential backoff with jitter and capped retries for transient errors like rate limits and network timeouts.
practices.prior_belief: Implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries of transient errors (network timeouts, 5xx server errors, rate limits), cap max retries, and make write operations idempotent (use upserts or deterministic document IDs) to safely retry.

practices.practice: When seeding or upserting many documents, use bulkWrite or batched upserts with reasonable batch sizes (and ordered=false where appropriate) to improve throughput and tolerate per-document failures.
practices.prior_belief: When seeding/upserting many documents with embeddings, use bulkWrite / bulk upsert operations with ordered=false and reasonable batch sizes to improve throughput and tolerate per-document failures without aborting the whole batch.
practices.source_name: Manage a document in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (bulkWrite guidance)

practices.practice: Store embeddings as numeric vectors (not strings); consider index-time compression options such as half-precision (fp16) or product quantization to reduce vector-index memory while validating recall.
practices.prior_belief: Store embeddings as float32 (not string) and, if supported by the server, use a native vector field type rather than an array of numbers to take advantage of vector indexes and store size/perf optimizations.

practices.practice: Protect the database with network controls: prefer Private Endpoint / VNet integration, disable public network access when possible, and narrow firewall allowed IPs to management/CI only.
practices.prior_belief: Protect the DocumentDB endpoint with network controls: restrict allowed client IPs, use VNet/private endpoints or firewalls, and avoid exposing the database publicly without IP restrictions.

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (managed identity) + RBAC for authentication rather than embedding admin passwords in app config; use per-app least-privilege secondary users if SCRAM is required.
Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs, analyze them in Log Analytics, and alert on cluster metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, connections) according to the cluster tier.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and record key metrics (query latency, vector index candidate counts, top-k retrieval time, index build time, failed upserts, embedding provider errors) and enable slow query profiling to detect regressions with production data.

practices.practice: Size storage and compute independently: pick Premium SSD v2 for new clusters and choose compute tier for required IOPS/bandwidth (size compute for throughput, not disk for IOPS).
practices.prior_belief: When creating collections, set appropriate storage and throughput settings for the expected workload (pre-create collections with the sample_healthcare_10 database, provisioned RU/throughput if applicable) and avoid creating very small collections that will be inefficient to index and serve vectors.

practices.practice: Use the $search aggregation stage with cosmosSearch (not other vendor-specific vector syntax) to perform kNN vector queries and return searchScore via $meta when needed.

Tune connection-pool settings to the deployment model: in serverless set small maxPoolSize (3–5), minPoolSize=0 and initialize the client outside the handler; in long-running servers set larger pools and pre-warm via minPoolSize.
For local development use the DocumentDB Gateway image on port 10260 with TLS and env-driven configuration; never default tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true in application code.
Manage index lifecycle safely: inventory indexes, hide an index to validate, then drop if unused; track per-collection index budget and drop unused indexes.
Use deterministic document IDs or unique constraints (use _id or a canonical hash) so upserts are idempotent and you avoid duplicate formulary entries.
practices.prior_belief: Use deterministic document IDs (e.g., hash of canonicalized drug name + normalized fields) or unique constraints to prevent accidental duplicate formulary entries and make upserts idempotent.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

practices.practice: Avoid full-collection scans for similarity by ensuring the vector index exists, matches the embedding dimensions/similarity, and verifying plans with explain; if index is not available, fail or limit candidate size rather than performing an unbounded scan.

When combining vector and lexical/full-text retrieval, prefer Azure DocumentDB's textSearch / createSearchIndexes instead of the community $text index for richer text options and to enable hybrid retrieval patterns.
For production index memory savings, prefer half-precision (fp16) indexing first and product quantization when more compression is needed, validating recall with an A/B test.
Use driver and app-level instrumentation (slow-query logs, searchScore candidate counts, index build times) and alert thresholds to detect regressions in vector retrieval and index health.
Prefer initializing MongoClient outside of request handlers (including FastAPI startup) so the same client/pool is reused by incoming requests and background tasks.

Fail early and surface clear errors when embedding dimensions or index parameters mismatch the stored vectors (e.g., check embedding length at ingest and abort if it does not match expected dimension).
When using serverless deployments, keep minPoolSize low, maxPoolSize small, and maxIdleTimeMS short to avoid idle connections consuming server resources across many short-lived instances.
When changing embedding models or normalization strategy, bump an embeddingVersion and plan a reindex/backfill and index rebuild to avoid mixing incompatible vectors.
Use the DocumentDB MCP tools to inspect collections, indexes, and explain plans during development and verification steps.

Rate-limit and cache calls to external embedding providers, and handle 429s with backoff; (no Azure DocumentDB public guidance found — this is prior knowledge about embedding providers, not DocumentDB itself).
practices.prior_belief: Rate-limit and batch calls to the external embedding provider (e.g., OpenAI): cache embeddings for identical inputs, and back off on 429/429-like responses to avoid bursting through provider quotas during seeding or requests.

practices.practice: Redact or avoid logging full clinical intent texts and embedding vectors in persistent logs; treat clinical queries as sensitive (no Azure DocumentDB public guidance found specific to PHI in query logs).
practices.prior_belief: Protect logs and error traces so they do not contain full user clinical intents or embedding vectors (PII/PHI); treat clinical query text as sensitive and redact it from persistent logs unless explicitly allowed and encrypted.
